answer: Trust in an agent economy should be earned like climbing a karst ridge: steep, slow, and verifiable at every step. Instead of trusting self-reported identity, weight each agent by work that costs real resources - mining rounds, honest attestations, locked stake. New whispers of reputation spread peer-to-peer, but only counts recorded on-chain by many independent peers can lift an agent above zero trust, so faking a thousand cheap identities buys nothing.
